title_seen: S2TA: Exploiting Structured Sparsity for Energy-Efficient Mobile CNN Acceleration
work_done: Proposes Density Bound Block (DBB) sparsity for static weights and dynamically pruned activations, and S2TA, an INT8 systolic-array accelerator with time-unrolled tensor PEs exploiting joint weight/activation DBB.
advantages: DBB bounds non-zeros per block so the maximum workload is known at design time, enabling lean hardware; reports >2x speedup and energy reduction vs a zero-value-clock-gated systolic array in 16nm.
disadvantages: Activation DBB uses Dynamic Activation Pruning (Top-NNZ), which is lossy (MobileNetV1 4/8 DAP on point-wise layers: 71% to 56.1% before retraining); evaluated by RTL simulation and ASIC flow (16nm/65nm), not on an FPGA.
relevance: Closest prior work: structured weight sparsity plus activation sparsity on an INT8 systolic array with a design-time workload bound; contrast with V3's lossless activation skipping bounded by the dense schedule.
read_locator: full text: abstract, Sec. 3.1, Sec. 4, Sec. 5.1 (DAP), Sec. 7 (methodology)

title_seen: An Efficient Hardware Accelerator for Structured Sparse Convolutional Neural Networks on FPGAs
work_done: Uses shape-wise structured pruning and a sparse-wise dataflow that skips MAC cycles with zero weights, with a Vector Generator Module matching sparse weight indices to activations; implemented on a Xilinx ZCU102.
advantages: Shape-wise pruning shares indices across kernels so PU load is balanced; reports 987 img/s (AlexNet) and 48 img/s (VGG-16) and 1.5x-6.7x speedup over prior FPGA CNN accelerators.
disadvantages: Zero activations are clock/zero-gated to save energy rather than skipped for speedup; evaluated on AlexNet and VGG-16 (ImageNet) on a ZCU102 with 16-bit and 8-bit variants.
relevance: Closest FPGA prior work for static structured weight skipping on a Zynq UltraScale+ device; V3's structured weight skip is positioned against it.

title_seen: Efficient Layer-Wise N:M Sparse CNN Accelerator with Flexible SPEC: Sparse Processing Element Clusters
work_done: Designs sparse PE clusters (SPEC) for layer-wise N:M weight sparsity (N:16 channel-wise) and builds input-, output- and input-output-channel-sparse accelerators in Verilog on Xilinx ZCU102 and VCU118.
advantages: Supports variable N per layer and variable sparse dimensions; reports Top-1 accuracy with N:16 50% sparsity close to dense for AlexNet, VGG-16, ResNet-18/50 and the best power efficiency among compared sparse accelerators.
disadvantages: Exploits weight sparsity only (one-sided for the ISA/OSA variants); evaluated on ImageNet-scale CNNs at 200 MHz on ZCU102/VCU118, not on smaller edge devices.
relevance: N:M structured weight sparsity on a Xilinx FPGA; a direct reference point for V3's static structured weight skip and per-layer sparsity choice.

title_seen: Cnvlutin: Ineffectual-Neuron-Free Deep Neural Network Computing
work_done: Proposes CNV, a value-based accelerator that eliminates multiplications with zero-valued activations using hierarchical data-parallel units whose lane groups proceed independently and a co-designed storage format.
advantages: No accuracy loss; improves performance 1.24x-1.55x (1.37x average) over a state-of-the-art accelerator with 4.49% area overhead, and 1.52x with a broader ineffectual-value policy.
disadvantages: Gains are data-dependent on activation zeros; evaluated against a DaDianNao-style baseline for image-classification DNNs (abstract does not report an FPGA or silicon implementation).
relevance: Classic activation zero-skipping reference; V3's all-zero K-step skipping is a coarse-grained, bounded variant of this idea.

title_seen: HPIPE: Heterogeneous Layer-Pipelined and Sparse-Aware CNN Inference for FPGAs
work_done: A network compiler and layer-pipelined FPGA architecture that builds custom hardware per CNN layer with zero-weight skipping, balancing per-layer throughput by splitting channels against a DSP target.
advantages: Sparse ResNet-50 (85% sparse) reaches 4550 images/s at batch 1 on a Stratix 10 2800; the compiler's analytic throughput model is within 1% of actual throughput after accounting for weight partitioning.
disadvantages: All experiments use 16-bit fixed point; targets a large Intel Stratix 10 and a layer-per-hardware pipeline that needs the whole network to fit on chip.
relevance: Static compile-time zero-weight skipping with an accurate throughput model on FPGA; closest to V3's compile-time-known structured weight skip schedule.
read_locator: full text: abstract, Sec. II-B, Sec. IV (balancing, 1% model), Sec. VI-VII

title_seen: Cambricon-X: An Accelerator for Sparse Neural Networks
work_done: PE-based accelerator for sparse NNs in which an Indexing Module selects and transfers the neurons matching each PE's compressed, irregular synapses, with PEs computing asynchronously.
advantages: 16 PEs reach up to 544 GOP/s in 6.38 mm2 and 954 mW at 65 nm; on average 7.23x speedup and 6.43x energy saving over a state-of-the-art NN accelerator on sparse networks.
disadvantages: Exploits weight sparsity (activations via indexing, not zero-skipping); ASIC (65 nm) evaluation only.
relevance: Classic weight-sparsity accelerator; contrast with V3's structured, statically scheduled weight skipping without a runtime indexing module.

title_seen: SCNN: An Accelerator for Compressed-sparse Convolutional Neural Networks
work_done: Accelerator that keeps both zero-pruned weights and ReLU-zero activations compressed and computes their Cartesian product in a multiplier array with a scatter accumulator array.
advantages: Exploits two-sided sparsity; reports 2.7x performance and 2.3x energy over a comparably provisioned dense accelerator across AlexNet, GoogLeNet and VGGNet.
disadvantages: Evaluated with a cycle-level simulator and 16nm synthesis; intra-PE fragmentation and inter-PE barrier load imbalance limit speedup (under 20% multiplier utilization in late GoogLeNet modules), and it is less efficient than dense above about 83% density.
relevance: Two-sided sparsity reference whose load imbalance and data-dependent runtime motivate V3's bounded, statically scheduled approach.

title_seen: Bit-Tactical: A Software/Hardware Approach to Exploiting Value and Bit Sparsity in Neural Networks
work_done: Accelerator where weight sparsity is exploited by a static scheduling middleware plus a lightweight sparse shuffling network (two small multiplexers per activation input), with back-ends that target bit-sparsity in activations.
advantages: Static weight scheduling avoids dynamic runtime routing/matching of values; targeting activation bit-sparsity avoids handling the dynamic whole-value sparse stream and uncovers more ineffectual work.
disadvantages: The abstract reports only qualitative comparisons (outperforms other sparse accelerators); hardware-only evaluation scope (no FPGA mentioned in the abstract).
relevance: Static (compile-time) weight-skip scheduling and zero-bit activation skipping; prior art for V3's static skip schedule.

title_seen: SparTen: A Sparse Tensor Accelerator for Convolutional Neural Networks
work_done: Two-sided sparse CNN accelerator with native sparse inner-join support and greedy balancing (software or hybrid) that groups filters by density to address systematic load imbalance.
advantages: Addresses SCNN's overheads and supports non-unit-stride convolutions; simulations show 4.7x, 1.8x and 3x over dense, one-sided sparse and SCNN, and an FPGA implementation shows 4.3x and 1.9x over dense and one-sided.
disadvantages: Runtime depends on data sparsity and needs balancing to limit imbalance; main results are simulation, with an FPGA implementation reported for a subset of comparisons.
relevance: Shows load imbalance is inherent to two-sided sparsity; contrast for V3's dense-bounded activation skip.

title_seen: NullHop: A Flexible Convolutional Neural Network Accelerator Based on Sparse Representations of Feature Maps
work_done: CNN accelerator that skips zero activations using a sparsity-map plus non-zero-value feature-map encoding, supporting 1x1 to 7x7 kernels; implemented on a Zynq 7100 FPGA and as a 28nm ASIC design.
advantages: Over 98% MAC utilization and 368% efficiency (ASIC post-synthesis, VGG19) by exploiting activation sparsity; reduces external memory transfers; FPGA version classifies at more than 8 FPS at 60 MHz.
disadvantages: Pipeline is data-dependent; FPGA version limited to 60 MHz by routing and FC layers run on the ARM CPU; 16-bit fixed point; ASIC numbers are post-synthesis simulation.
relevance: FPGA activation zero-skipping on a Zynq SoC; contrast with V3's coarse K-step skip with a dense worst-case bound.
read_locator: full text: abstract, Sec. IV (FPGA implementation, Tables II-III), Sec. V (VGG results)

title_seen: EIE: Efficient Inference Engine on Compressed Deep Neural Network
work_done: Inference engine for Deep-Compression models (pruned, weight-shared) that performs sparse matrix-vector multiplication on FC layers and skips zero activations from ReLU.
advantages: Reports 120x energy saving from SRAM residency, 10x from sparsity, 8x from weight sharing and 3x from activation zero-skipping; 189x/13x faster than CPU/GPU on nine DNN benchmarks.
disadvantages: Targets fully-connected (sparse matrix-vector) layers rather than convolutions; 45nm ASIC evaluation.
relevance: Classic weight-and-activation sparsity engine; background for V3's sparsity related work, not a CNN-conv comparison point.
